mission: Produce a forensic dossier for each of the 8 pinned capture-envelope bypasses in packages/capture-envelope/test/redteamBypassF22.test.ts (B1 blur+grain, B2 bimodal exposure, B3 strobing, B4 upscale, B5 tiny subject, B6 rotate-tag normalization, FR1 low-texture false reject, B7 crop-jitter shake): measure current signals, actually run Linux-runnable downstream pipeline stages on each bypass clip, identify the observable signal that would have prevented the failure, and classify each bypass as A logic bug / B normalization bug / C missing pre-capture signal computable today / D threshold needs real labels / E fundamentally unobservable pre-capture.
method: Harness packages/swing-lab/src/g06F22Dossiers.ts synthesizes each pinned bypass clip with ffmpeg using the exact recipes pinned in redteamBypassF22.test.ts (plus realism variants where the exact pinned construction confounds the intended failure mode with a frozen background), then for each clip measures: (1) the full capture-envelope verdict via measureClip + evaluateCaptureEnvelope (thresholds v0.3-provisional); (2) the pose-free downstream OOD gate extractFrameStats -> evaluateFrameAnalyzability; (3) downstream ball-candidate generation via tools/paddle-lab/ball_candidates.py (candidates/frame, chronic-cell fraction, zero-candidate frames); (4) a panel of candidate preventive signals computable pre-capture with the same 4fps/320px grayscale sampling used by clipProbe (denoise-survival ratio of Laplacian variance, multi-scale detail ratio 640/320, clipped-pixel fraction, per-frame off-band luma fraction, top-1% edge gradient, contrast-normalized frame diff, moving-subject height fraction from frame-diff bounding box). Pose-gated stages (Apple Vision pose, canonical cascade) are unavailable on Linux and are reported as NOT MEASURED, not fabricated.
dataset_scope_and_grouping: 17 clips total: 8 exact pinned bypass constructions, 2 moving realism variants (b2_bimodal_moving, b5_tiny_subject_moving_bg), and 7 controls (control_base synthetic scene, control_b1_blur_only, control_b4_true240, control_b5_big_subject, control_fr1_blurred, control_b7_real_shake and control_b7_real_unshaken derived from non-held-out real clip afn-sasebo-rally1). All synthetic clips are 4s @ 30fps 1280x720 (or as pinned). Grouping is per-bypass: each bypass clip is compared against its matched control.
holdout_statement: Held-out cases wm-dink-01 and afn-vic-rally1 were not read, listed, referenced, or used in any way. The only real footage used is afn-sasebo-rally1 (non-held-out).

B1_blur_plus_grain.input_condition: Heavily Gaussian-blurred scene (sigma large enough that blur-only fails) with synthetic film grain overlaid; grain restores high-frequency energy.
B1_blur_plus_grain.current_signals_measured: laplacianVarianceMedian 173.8 (>= 100 threshold, SUPPORTED); control_b1_blur_only without grain measures 5.1 (UNSUPPORTED). All other dimensions SUPPORTED.
B1_blur_plus_grain.why_envelope_passes: Raw Laplacian variance measures total high-frequency energy and cannot distinguish sensor/overlay noise from real scene detail; grain alone lifts 5.1 -> 173.8.
B1_blur_plus_grain.downstream_failure_measured: Ball candidate stage floods: 39.93 candidates/frame (vs 16.53 control_base) with chronicCellFraction 0.988 (vs 0.014 control) — 98.8% of grid cells show chronic false motion activity, drowning real ball candidates in grain-induced noise. OOD gate does not catch it (ANALYZABLE).
B1_blur_plus_grain.preventive_signal: Denoise-survival ratio: Laplacian variance after light temporal/spatial denoise divided by raw. Measured 0.126 for b1_blur_grain vs 0.792-1.089 for all genuine-content clips (min genuine 0.339 on real footage) — a >2.6x separation gap.
B1_blur_plus_grain.needs_learned_calibration: Threshold placement (e.g. 0.126 vs 0.339) has a wide gap on this data but should be calibrated on labeled real noisy-phone footage before locking.
B1_blur_plus_grain.current_threshold_identifiable_from_data: The lapVar>=100 threshold is v0.3-provisional and is not identifiable as a noise-robust boundary from current data; it conflates blur and grain.
B1_blur_plus_grain.classification_rationale: A concrete pre-capture signal (denoise-survival ratio) computable today with existing ffmpeg sampling cleanly separates the bypass from all 9 genuine-content clips measured; calibration refinement is secondary (D).

B2_bimodal_exposure.input_condition: Half the frame crushed to near-black (luma ~ val/16), half blown to near-white (luma ~ 220+val/16); spatial mean lands mid-band.
B2_bimodal_exposure.current_signals_measured: brightnessMeanLuma 122.4 (in 60-200 band, SUPPORTED) despite clippedPixelFraction 0.997 (99.7% of pixels outside [16,235] usable range). Exact pinned clip: envelope SUPPORTED overall.
B2_bimodal_exposure.why_envelope_passes: Brightness check uses only the spatial mean; a bimodal histogram with almost no mid-tone pixels averages into the supported band.
B2_bimodal_exposure.downstream_failure_measured: Exact pinned clip is additionally frozen, so the OOD gate rejects it as still_image_video (confounder). Realism variant b2_bimodal_moving (same lut, moving scene) passes the envelope (SUPPORTED), passes the OOD gate (ANALYZABLE), and starves the ball stage: 0.03 candidates/frame with 115/118 zero-candidate frames vs 16.53/frame and 0 zero frames on control_base — near-total tracking starvation with no gate firing.
B2_bimodal_exposure.preventive_signal: Clipped-pixel fraction (pixels outside [16,235]): 0.997 on both B2 clips vs <= 0.051 on all 15 other clips.
B2_bimodal_exposure.needs_learned_calibration: Minimal — the measured separation is 0.997 vs 0.051; a conservative bound (e.g. reject > 0.5) is defensible, but band edges should be confirmed on real backlit footage.
B2_bimodal_exposure.current_threshold_identifiable_from_data: The mean-luma 60-200 band cannot express this failure at all; no setting of the existing threshold fixes it.
B2_bimodal_exposure.classification_rationale: Histogram-shape signal computable today from the same sampled frames; the existing mean-based check is structurally blind to it.

B3_strobing_exposure.input_condition: Frames alternate between near-black and near-white; temporal mean luma lands mid-band.
B3_strobing_exposure.current_signals_measured: brightnessMeanLuma in-band -> brightness dimension SUPPORTED despite offBandFrameFraction 1.0 (100% of individual frames outside the band) and brightnessStdLuma 109.0. Overall envelope happens to be UNSUPPORTED, but only via side-effects: laplacianVarianceMedian 0.0 (solid frames) and meanAbsFrameDiff 101.7 (camera_motion).
B3_strobing_exposure.why_envelope_passes: The brightness dimension itself passes because it averages luma over time; the clip is only rejected by dimensions that measure something else. A milder strobe that keeps some texture and lower flicker amplitude would evade all dimensions.
B3_strobing_exposure.downstream_failure_measured: OOD gate rejects with solid_color_frames; ball candidates 0.0/frame. For this exact construction downstream gates do fire, but for the wrong reasons — the brightness gate never sees the strobe.
B3_strobing_exposure.preventive_signal: Per-frame off-band fraction: fraction of sampled frames whose per-frame mean luma is outside [60,200]. Measured 1.0 for B3 vs 0.0 for all 16 other clips. brightnessStdLuma (109.0 vs <= 2.32 elsewhere) is an equivalent already-computed signal that is currently unused by evaluateCaptureEnvelope.
B3_strobing_exposure.needs_learned_calibration: Off-band-fraction threshold is near-trivial (1.0 vs 0.0 measured); a flicker-amplitude threshold for milder strobes would need labeled real footage.
B3_strobing_exposure.current_threshold_identifiable_from_data: The mean-based band is identifiable for static lighting but structurally cannot encode temporal exposure instability.
B3_strobing_exposure.classification_rationale: The clip already carries brightnessStdLuma in measurements — the signal exists and is computed today but is never evaluated; adding a per-frame/temporal-variance check is a pre-capture-computable fix. (Borders on A since the measured std is silently discarded.)

B4_upscale.input_condition: True 240p content upscaled to 1280x720; container metadata reports 720p short side.
B4_upscale.current_signals_measured: shortSidePx 720 (SUPPORTED); laplacianVarianceMedian 608.0 (SUPPORTED). control_b4_true240 (same content at native 240p) is UNSUPPORTED purely on resolution metadata.
B4_upscale.why_envelope_passes: Resolution check trusts container dimensions; upscaling preserves enough low-frequency edge energy at the 320px sampling width that Laplacian variance stays high.
B4_upscale.downstream_failure_measured: OOD gate ANALYZABLE; ball stage saturates at 40.0 candidates/frame (vs 16.53 control_base, 15.17 true-240p control) with chronicCellFraction 0.061 — upscaling ringing/aliasing inflates false candidates ~2.4x while genuinely carrying only 240p of information for any later fine-grained stage.
B4_upscale.preventive_signal: Multi-scale detail ratio (lapVar at 640px sampling / lapVar at 320px): 0.318 for b4_upscaled_240p vs 0.742 for native-720p control_base and 0.756/0.759 for other native clips. Caveat: control_b4_true240 measures 0.333 — the ratio measures effective detail, not the upscale operation itself, so it detects 'content has less detail than claimed resolution' rather than 'was upscaled'.
B4_upscale.needs_learned_calibration: Yes. The 0.32-vs-0.74 gap is clean on synthetic clips, but real phone footage spans a continuum of optics/compression detail; the reject boundary needs labeled real captures at known native resolutions.
B4_upscale.current_threshold_identifiable_from_data: The 720p metadata threshold is identifiable as a metadata check but cannot be made robust to upscaling at any setting.
B4_upscale.classification_rationale: The preventive signal is computable today (C-eligible), but unlike B1/B2 the safe threshold genuinely depends on the real-footage detail distribution; setting it from synthetic data alone would risk false rejects of soft-optics genuine 720p+.

B5_tiny_subject.input_condition: Subject occupies ~0.6-12.5% of frame height (far below the 25% pose pixel-height threshold); video-only statistics are all healthy.
B5_tiny_subject.current_signals_measured: All 7 video dimensions SUPPORTED; player_pixel_height and player_visibility are NOT_MEASURED because no pose pass has run. evaluateCaptureEnvelope reports overall SUPPORTED with notMeasured [player_pixel_height, player_visibility].
B5_tiny_subject.why_envelope_passes: Overall status is the worst of measured dimensions; NOT_MEASURED dimensions cannot worsen it. Callers that treat overall SUPPORTED as a full green light (without checking notMeasured) admit clips the pose dimensions were designed to reject.
B5_tiny_subject.downstream_failure_measured: Exact pinned clip is frozen and caught as still_image_video (confounder). Realism variant b5_tiny_subject_moving_bg (moving 64x36 subject on the moving base scene) passes envelope (SUPPORTED) and OOD gate (ANALYZABLE) and produces a normal-looking 16.5 candidates/frame — nothing downstream on Linux flags it. The actual failure (pose extraction on a 36px-tall subject) is pose-gated and could not be measured on Linux; it is the documented rationale for the 0.25 pixel-height threshold, not remeasured here.
B5_tiny_subject.preventive_signal: Two-layer: (1) contract fix — overall verdict must distinguish SUPPORTED from SUPPORTED_WITH_UNMEASURED_DIMENSIONS or callers must be required to consume notMeasured; (2) a pose-free proxy exists: moving-subject height fraction from frame-diff bounding boxes measures 0.006-0.125 on B5 clips vs 0.229-1.0 on adequate-subject clips (control_b5_big_subject measures 0.061 due to slow motion, so this proxy is noisy and needs calibration).
B5_tiny_subject.signal_exists_pre_capture: The contract fix requires no new signal. The motion-based subject-size proxy is computable pre-capture but noisy; the true signal (pose bbox) exists on-device pre-capture on iPhone (Vision runs live) but not in this Linux pipeline.
B5_tiny_subject.needs_learned_calibration: Contract fix: no. Motion-proxy threshold: yes, on labeled real footage.
B5_tiny_subject.current_threshold_identifiable_from_data: The 0.25 pose-height threshold itself is documented as provisional from Wave-earlier pose failure analysis; it is not re-derivable from this experiment.
B5_tiny_subject.classification_rationale: The primary defect is the verdict contract: a clip with the critical dimensions unmeasured is reported with the same overall status as a fully-verified clip. That is a logic/contract bug independent of any new signal.

B6_rotate_tag_normalization.input_condition: Identical pixel content delivered with a rotation metadata tag (portrait container + rotate tag) instead of baked-in orientation.
B6_rotate_tag_normalization.current_signals_measured: laplacianVarianceMedian drops from 376.4 (untagged control_base) to 266.0 (rotate-tagged) — a 29% change from metadata alone, because sampling scales to a fixed 320px width of the display-rotated frame, changing the effective sampling resolution per axis.
B6_rotate_tag_normalization.why_envelope_passes: Both sides of this construction currently pass (266 >= 100), but the same normalization inconsistency moves clips near the threshold across the boundary in either direction depending on orientation tagging — the measurement is not rotation-invariant.
B6_rotate_tag_normalization.downstream_failure_measured: OOD gate ANALYZABLE; ball candidates 34.99/frame vs 16.53 on the untagged identical content — the different effective sampling scale materially changes downstream candidate statistics for identical pixels.
B6_rotate_tag_normalization.preventive_signal: Normalize sampling by the long side (or by total pixel count) of the display-oriented frame instead of fixed width. Verified: long-side-normalized Laplacian variance measures 377 on the rotate-tagged clip vs 376.4 untagged (<0.2% difference), restoring rotation invariance.
B6_rotate_tag_normalization.needs_learned_calibration: No. This is a deterministic normalization fix; existing thresholds keep their meaning for landscape content.
B6_rotate_tag_normalization.current_threshold_identifiable_from_data: The threshold is fine; the measurement feeding it is orientation-dependent.
B6_rotate_tag_normalization.classification_rationale: Pure normalization bug: identical pixels yield different measurements depending on container rotation metadata; a long-side normalization verified in this experiment removes the discrepancy.

FR1_low_texture_false_reject.input_condition: Perfectly sharp but low-texture scene (flat walls/court, few edges); genuinely analyzable footage.
FR1_low_texture_false_reject.current_signals_measured: laplacianVarianceMedian 78.6 < 100 -> motion_blur DEGRADED (false reject). control_fr1_blurred (actually blurred version) measures 5.8 (correct reject).
FR1_low_texture_false_reject.why_envelope_fails_here: Laplacian variance conflates 'sharp but textureless' with 'blurred': it measures texture quantity, not focus quality.
FR1_low_texture_false_reject.downstream_failure_measured: OOD gate: ANALYZABLE. Ball candidates: 0.02/frame — with this synthetic low-texture construction the ball stage also starves, so on THIS clip the reject is arguably beneficial for ball tracking; but the pose/form-analysis path (not measurable on Linux) does not require background texture, so the false reject remains real for pose-only use. Honest note: this experiment cannot quantify the pose-path cost on Linux.
FR1_low_texture_false_reject.preventive_signal: Sharpness measured on detected edges only, e.g. top-1% edge gradient magnitude: 89.0 for sharp low-texture vs 66.3 for its blurred control (separates within the pair), while texture-rich sharp clips measure 148-239. A ratio-based or edge-conditional sharpness metric decouples focus from texture quantity.
FR1_low_texture_false_reject.needs_learned_calibration: Yes. The sharp-vs-blurred separation within low-texture content (89 vs 66) is much narrower than across texture levels; a robust boundary requires labeled real low-texture captures.
FR1_low_texture_false_reject.current_threshold_identifiable_from_data: The lapVar>=100 threshold cannot be set anywhere that both accepts sharp low-texture and rejects blurred textured footage — the metric is one-dimensional over a two-dimensional (focus x texture) space.
FR1_low_texture_false_reject.classification_rationale: An edge-conditional sharpness signal is computable today, but its measured margin on low-texture content is narrow (89 vs 66); locking a threshold without labeled real footage would be threshold-gaming. Needs real labels.

B7_crop_jitter_shake.input_condition: Handheld-shake simulation via crop-window jitter on synthetic low-contrast content; nominally equivalent shake applied to real footage is rejected.
B7_crop_jitter_shake.current_signals_measured: b7_synthetic_shake: meanAbsFrameDiff 13.05 <= 33 -> SUPPORTED. control_b7_real_shake (same nominal jitter on real afn-sasebo-rally1 footage): 35.51 -> DEGRADED. control_b7_real_unshaken: 8.97 -> SUPPORTED.
B7_crop_jitter_shake.why_envelope_passes: meanAbsFrameDiff measures shake x scene contrast, not shake magnitude: the same geometric camera motion produces 13.05 on low-contrast synthetic content and 35.51 on real content. Low-contrast shaky footage passes; the threshold is content-dependent.
B7_crop_jitter_shake.downstream_failure_measured: b7_synthetic_shake: OOD ANALYZABLE, 24.12 candidates/frame vs 16.53 unshaken control — shake inflates false motion candidates ~1.5x while passing all gates. control_b7_real_shake inflates to 39.48/frame with chronicCellFraction 0.146 (vs 0.196 unshaken real, 0.014 synthetic base).
B7_crop_jitter_shake.preventive_signal: Contrast-normalized frame difference (meanAbsFrameDiff / spatial luma std): 0.201 for synthetic shake vs 0.054 unshaken synthetic; 0.634 for real shake vs 0.164 unshaken real — a consistent ~3.7-3.9x shaken/unshaken ratio across content types, unlike the raw diff whose absolute value is content-dependent. Full fix is block-motion/global-registration estimation, also computable on the same sampled frames.
B7_crop_jitter_shake.needs_learned_calibration: Yes for the normalized-diff threshold (the shaken/unshaken ratio is stable but absolute band placement needs real labeled handheld footage); a registration-based pixel-displacement estimate could use a physically-motivated threshold with less calibration.
B7_crop_jitter_shake.current_threshold_identifiable_from_data: The <=33 raw-diff threshold is not identifiable as a shake threshold from data because the quantity it bounds is not shake.
B7_crop_jitter_shake.classification_rationale: Contrast-normalized (or registration-based) motion is computable today from the same sampling and, in this experiment, gives consistent shaken/unshaken separation across synthetic and real content where the raw metric contradicts itself; final band placement is a secondary D.

findings: Counts: of 8 pinned bypasses, 5 exact constructions pass the envelope overall (B1, B2, B4, B5, B6), 1 falsely rejects (FR1), 1 passes only its targeted dimension while other dimensions incidentally reject (B3), and 1 passes while its real-footage equivalent is rejected (B7).

Downstream (Linux-measurable, 118 frames/clip): 3 bypasses cause ball-candidate flooding (B1 39.93/frame with 98.8% chronic cells; B4 40.0/frame; B7 24.12/frame vs 16.53 baseline) and 2 cause near-total candidate starvation (B2-moving 0.03/frame with 115/118 empty frames; FR1 0.02/frame). B5-moving and B6 pass all Linux-measurable downstream stages; their real failure surface (pose extraction / threshold-boundary drift) is pose-gated or boundary-dependent.

Confounder found and controlled: the exact pinned B2 and B5 constructions freeze the background and are caught by the OOD still-image check for the wrong reason; moving realism variants confirm the intended bypass survives all gates.

The envelope already computes brightnessStdLuma but never evaluates it (B3); and the overall verdict silently equates 'all dimensions pass' with 'all measured dimensions pass' (B5) — two defects fixable without any new signal.
Classification tally: A=1 (B5), B=1 (B6), C=4 (B1, B2, B3, B7), D=2 (B4, FR1), E=0. No bypass is fundamentally unobservable pre-capture.

Not measured (honest gaps): Apple Vision pose, canonical stroke cascade, and iPhone capture behavior — all pose-gated or platform-gated off Linux. B5's and FR1's pose-path consequences are therefore documented from prior-wave rationale, not remeasured.
verdict_rationale: All 8 dossiers are complete with measured envelope signals, actually-executed Linux downstream stages (OOD gate + ball candidates, 118 frames/clip, 17 clips), matched controls, and verified preventive signals (including a verified normalization fix for B6 and >2x measured separations for B1/B2/B3/B7 candidate signals). ORANGE rather than GREEN because: (a) the pose-gated downstream stages could not be run on Linux, so B5/FR1 downstream costs rest partly on prior-wave documentation; (b) all preventive-signal separations were measured on synthetic constructions plus one real clip (afn-sasebo-rally1) — threshold placement for the C/D items still requires labeled real footage; (c) classifications are evidence-backed but the D items are explicitly not resolvable without new labels.
